    easyui

    Buttons, sliders, text inputs, radio buttons and more for mosWM apps, in one header. Include easyui.h.

    easyui opens one window, keeps a list of widgets, draws them, and turns mouse and keyboard events into callbacks. Text is smooth, anti-aliased Inter drawn by the same OpenType renderer mosWM uses. Its colours follow the MOSdesk theme picked in Settings > Appearance, and they change while the app is running when the user picks another theme.

    Functionseasyui.initeasyui.runeasyui.updateeasyui.quiteasyui.settitleeasyui.widtheasyui.heighteasyui.windoweasyui.redraweasyui.setdarkmodeeasyui.setaccenteasyui.accenteasyui.themeeasyui.loadfonteasyui.setsmoothtexteasyui.smoothtexteasyui.createbuttoneasyui.createlabeleasyui.createslidereasyui.createcheckboxeasyui.createradioeasyui.createtoggleeasyui.createtextinputeasyui.createprogresseasyui.createdropdowneasyui.createlistboxeasyui.createpaneleasyui.createimageeasyui.createcanvaseasyui.createseparatoreasyui.removeeasyui.recallfunceasyui.currenteasyui.settexteasyui.gettexteasyui.setvalueeasyui.getvalueeasyui.setrangeeasyui.setstepeasyui.additemeasyui.clearitemseasyui.getitemeasyui.itemcounteasyui.setenabledeasyui.setvisibleeasyui.setpositioneasyui.setsizeeasyui.setanchoreasyui.setcoloreasyui.settextsizeeasyui.setaligneasyui.setstyleeasyui.setpasswordeasyui.setmaxlengtheasyui.setimageeasyui.setfocuseasyui.focusedeasyui.typeeasyui.getxeasyui.getyeasyui.getwidtheasyui.getheighteasyui.settimereasyui.stoptimereasyui.messageboxeasyui.pixelseasyui.fillrecteasyui.drawrecteasyui.fillroundrecteasyui.fillcircleeasyui.drawlineeasyui.drawtexteasyui.textwidtheasyui.drawpixelseasyui.addfonteasyui.setfonteasyui.setfontsizeeasyui.settextcoloreasyui.setbackgroundeasyui.setbordereasyui.setradiuseasyui.setpaddingeasyui.copystyleeasyui.drawtextfonteasyui.textwidthfonteasyui.setlookeasyui.lookeasyui.pickfileeasyui.savefileeasyui.pickfoldereasyui.pickedpatheasyui.mouse
    #include "easyui.h"

static int label1;

static void clicked(int value) {
    easyui.settext(label1, "Thanks!");
}

int main(void) {
    easyui.init("Hello", 320, 160);
    int button1 = easyui.createbutton(20, 20, 200, 40, "Click me!");
    label1 = easyui.createlabel(20, 80, 280, 24, "Nobody clicked yet");
    easyui.recallfunc(button1, ONCLICK, clicked);
    return easyui.run();
}

    Build it like any program (./build.sh hello.c), or open the Widgets (easyui) sample in Run Studio. examples/easyui-demo.c uses every widget.

    How it works

    • One object. Every function is called through easyui: easyui.createbutton(...), easyui.setvalue(...). It is a constant structure of function pointers, so it works the same from C and C++.
    • Widgets are ints. Each create... call returns a widget number (1 … 128), or 0 if there was no room. Keep it in an int and pass it to the other calls. Calls with an invalid widget do nothing.
    • Coordinates are pixels inside the window's content area: (0, 0) is the top-left corner below the title bar. Widgets are drawn in the order they were created, so create a panel before the widgets on it.
    • Callbacks take one int, the event's value (see Events). Register them with easyui.recallfunc. Inside a callback, easyui.current says which widget fired, so one function can serve several widgets.
    • The main loop is easyui.run. It handles events, runs timers, redraws only when something changed and sleeps between frames. Callbacks can change any widget; the window is repainted afterwards.
    • Memory. Widgets live in a fixed table (EASYUI_MAX_WIDGETS, 128). Widget text holds up to 127 bytes. List and dropdown items are copied to the heap and freed by clearitems and remove.

    Several source files

    The implementation is inside the header. In a program with more than one .c file, include easyui.h normally in one file, and in every other file write:

    #define EASYUI_NO_IMPLEMENTATION
#include "easyui.h"

    Events

    Pass one of these to recallfunc. The short names (ONCLICK) are macros for EASYUI_ONCLICK and friends; define EASYUI_NO_SHORT_NAMES before the include if they clash with your own names.

    EventWhenValue passed to the callback
    ONPRESSThe left mouse button goes down on the widget, or Space/Enter is pressed while it has focus1
    ONRELEASEThe button comes up again after an ONPRESS, wherever the pointer is0
    ONCLICKPressed and released on the same widget0
    ONCELike ONCLICK, but only the first time; the callback is then removed0
    ONCHANGEThe widget's value changed, by the user or by setvaluethe new value (see below)
    ONSUBMITEnter in a text input; Enter or a double-click in a list boxtext length, or the item index
    ONHOVERThe pointer moved onto the widget0
    ONLEAVEThe pointer moved off it0
    ONFOCUSIt got keyboard focus0
    ONBLURIt lost keyboard focus0
    ONKEYA key went down while it had focus (on EASYUI_WINDOW: any key)key | (modifiers << 8)
    ONDRAWCanvas only: draw your content now0
    ONFRAMEWindow only: once per frame, about 60 times a seconduptime in ms
    ONCLOSEWindow only: the close button was clicked0
    ONRESIZEWindow only: the window changed sizethe new width
    ONWHEELCanvas only: the mouse wheel turned over it1 up, -1 down

    ONCHANGE values by widget:

    WidgetValue
    Slider, progress barThe new value
    Checkbox, toggle1 checked / on, 0 not
    Radio button1 when it becomes selected, 0 when another in its group does
    Text inputThe text's new length (read the text with gettext)
    Dropdown, list boxIndex of the selected item

    Window events use EASYUI_WINDOW (0) as the widget:

    static void closing(int value) {
    easyui.messagebox("Not yet", "Save your work first.");   /* or easyui.quit() */
}
easyui.recallfunc(EASYUI_WINDOW, ONCLOSE, closing);

    Without an ONCLOSE callback, clicking the close button ends run().

    Keyboard

    Click a widget or press Tab (Shift+Tab backwards) to give it focus; a ring in the accent colour shows which one has it.

    WidgetKeys
    Button, checkbox, toggleSpace or Enter clicks it
    Radio buttonSpace selects; arrow keys move to the previous/next button of the same group and select it
    SliderArrows step by setstep (default 1); Home and End jump to the ends
    Text inputTyping, Backspace, Delete, Left, Right, Home, End; Enter submits; Escape leaves the field
    DropdownSpace or Enter opens it; Up and Down change the selection
    List boxUp and Down move the selection; Enter submits

    Key codes are USB HID usage codes. easyui.h defines the common ones: EASYUI_KEY_ENTER (40), _ESCAPE (41), _BACKSPACE (42), _TAB (43), _SPACE (44), _HOME (74), _DELETE (76), _END (77), _RIGHT (79), _LEFT (80), _DOWN (81), _UP (82). Letters are 4 (a) … 29 (z).

    Theme

    MOSdesk stores the chosen theme as an accent colour in 0:/programs/mosdesk/settings.dat. easyui reads it when the window opens and again twice a second, and repaints when it changes. Without MOSdesk (no settings file), the accent is MOSdesk's default blue, 0xFF3DAEE9.

    The other colours match mosWM: the light palette of its dialogs and the Settings app by default, or the dark palette of its menus and Files window after easyui.setdarkmode(1).

    ThemeAccent
    Blue0xFF59A6D8
    Teal0xFF48B8A5
    Copper0xFFD28C54
    Forest0xFF69A86A
    Rose0xFFD66B83
    Gold0xFFE1B64C

    Text

    easyui draws text the way mosWM does:

    • Smooth text (normal). easyui_text.h is a bundled copy of ttrend_outline, the anti-aliased OpenType/TrueType renderer mosWM uses (integer maths only, no libc). When the window opens, easyui loads the Inter fonts mosWM installs, 0:/programs/mosWM/assets/fonts/Inter-Regular.otf and Inter-Medium.otf. Text size 1 is 12 px Inter Regular; size 2 and up is 8 × size px Inter Medium, the same sizes mosWM uses for its own text. Text is proportional: wrapping, alignment and the text-input caret are measured with the real glyph widths.
    • Bitmap fallback. If neither font can be read (mosWM is not installed, or the files are missing), or after easyui.setsmoothtext(0), text uses the 8 × 8 bitmap font mosWM falls back to, scaled by the text size.
    • Your own font. easyui.loadfont loads any .otf or .ttf file instead.

    Run Studio's preview has the same Inter files at the same path, so smooth text looks the same there as on MOSdesk.

    include/easyui_text.h is generated from MOSdesk's mosdesk/libraries/ttrend_outline by tools/bundle-ttrend.py; do not edit it by hand.

    Styling widgets

    Every widget can have its own font, text size, text and background colour, border, corner radius and padding:

    int save = easyui.createbutton(20, 20, 160, 44, "Save");
easyui.setfont(save, EASYUI_FONT_MEDIUM);
easyui.setfontsize(save, 18);                 /* 18 px text */
easyui.setbackground(save, 0xFF2E7D32);       /* green; hover and pressed shades follow */
easyui.setradius(save, 12);
easyui.setborder(save, 0xFF1B5E20, 2);

    Pass EASYUI_WINDOW instead of a widget to set the default for every widget that has no setting of its own (setbackground(EASYUI_WINDOW, ...) colours the window itself):

    int mono = easyui.addfont("0:/programs/notes/Resources/Mono.ttf");
easyui.setfont(EASYUI_WINDOW, mono);          /* the whole app in Mono */
easyui.setfontsize(EASYUI_WINDOW, 14);

    A widget's own setting wins over the window's, which wins over the theme. 0 (colours, setfontsize) or -1 (setborder width, setradius, setpadding) goes back to the default. easyui.copystyle gives one widget another's whole style.

    CallButtonsLabelsText inputs, lists, dropdowns, panelsOthers
    setfont, setfontsizelabeltexttext and rowslabel text; canvases' drawtext
    settextcolorlabeltexttextlabel text
    setbackgroundfillbox behind the textfillbox behind (checkbox, radio, toggle, image, canvas); track (slider, progress)
    setborder, setradiusoutline, cornersoutline, cornersoutline, cornersoutline, corners
    setpaddingtext inset (8)text inset (0)text inset (8, rows 10)space before the box

    Looks: Modern and 2000s Aero

    When the user picks 2000s Aero under Settings > Appearance > Window style, easyui windows follow it: grey glass push buttons that turn light blue on hover, Windows 7 style check boxes, radio buttons, sunken text fields, a green progress bar, blue list selections and a white message box over a grey button strip. Like the accent colour, it changes while the app runs. easyui.setlook fixes one look for an app.

    File and folder pickers

    easyui.pickfile, easyui.savefile and easyui.pickfolder open a dialog over the window, in the current look: Home, its Documents, Pictures and Desktop folders and System on the left; Home, System and Up buttons and the current folder on top; the folder's contents in the middle (folders first); a name field and Cancel / Open (Save, Select) at the bottom. They return at once; the callback runs when the user is done, with 1 for a choice and 0 for Cancel or Escape, and easyui.pickedpath gives the path.

    static void opened(int chosen) {
    if (chosen) load_document(easyui.pickedpath());
}
easyui.pickfile("Open a note", 0, "txt;md", opened);
    Keys
    Up, DownMove the selection
    EnterOpen the selected folder, or choose (same as the main button)
    BackspaceUp one folder (in the save dialog: edit the name)
    EscapeCancel
    Double-clickOpen a folder, or choose a file

    While a picker is up the window's widgets ignore input; timers and ONFRAME keep running. One picker at a time.

    Limits

    LimitValue
    WidgetsEASYUI_MAX_WIDGETS (128)
    Fonts from addfontEASYUI_MAX_FONTS (8)
    Picker pathsEASYUI_PATH_MAX - 1 (255) bytes; 256 entries per folder
    Widget textEASYUI_TEXT_MAX - 1 (127) bytes
    TimersEASYUI_MAX_TIMERS (8)
    WindowsOne per program
    TextInter via the OpenType renderer (8 × 8 bitmap fallback); ASCII from the keyboard. No kerning or right-to-left text

    easyui.init

    int easyui.init(const char* title, int width, int height);

    Opens the app's window and loads the MOSdesk theme. Call it before creating any widget.

    ParameterDescription
    titleTitle bar text (63 bytes at most)
    width, heightContent size in pixels, at least 64 × 48

    Returns 1, or 0 if the window could not be created (no window manager running, or out of memory). Calling it again does nothing and returns 1.

    Example

    if (!easyui.init("Notes", 480, 320)) {
    mos_puts("Start MOSdesk first\n");
    return 1;
}

    easyui.run

    int easyui.run(void);

    Runs the app until the window is closed or easyui.quit is called, then closes the window.

    Returns 0, so return easyui.run(); ends main with exit code 0.

    Notes Each frame handles all pending window events, polls the theme, runs due timers, fires ONFRAME, repaints if anything changed and sleeps 16 ms.

    easyui.update

    int easyui.update(void);

    One frame of easyui.run without the sleep, for programs with their own loop.

    Returns 1 while the app should keep running, 0 once it is closing.

    Example

    while (easyui.update()) {
    simulate_step();
    mos_sleep(10);
}

    easyui.quit

    void easyui.quit(void);

    Makes run() return (and update() return 0) after the current frame.

    easyui.settitle

    void easyui.settitle(const char* title);

    Changes the window's title.

    easyui.width

    int easyui.width(void);

    Returns the current content width. It changes when the user resizes the window.

    easyui.height

    int easyui.height(void);

    Returns the current content height.

    easyui.window

    uint32_t easyui.window(void);

    Returns the mosWM window ID, for calls from window.h such as mos_window_set_flags.

    Example

    mos_window_set_resizable(easyui.window(), false);   /* fixed-size window */

    easyui.redraw

    void easyui.redraw(void);

    Asks for a repaint on the next frame. Only needed after changing something easyui cannot see, such as the pixels behind an image widget or the state a canvas draws.

    easyui.setdarkmode

    void easyui.setdarkmode(int on);

    Switches between the light palette (default) and the dark one. The accent colour is unchanged.

    Example

    easyui.recallfunc(dark_toggle, ONCHANGE, easyui.setdarkmode);

    easyui.setaccent

    void easyui.setaccent(uint32_t argb);

    Uses argb as the accent colour instead of MOSdesk's. Pass 0 to follow MOSdesk again.

    easyui.accent

    uint32_t easyui.accent(void);

    Returns the accent colour in use, as 0xFFRRGGBB. Use it to draw your own content in the theme colour.

    easyui.theme

    const easyui_theme_t* easyui.theme(void);

    Returns every colour easyui is using. The structure is read-only.

    FieldUsed for
    backgroundWindow content
    surfaceText inputs, lists, panels, slider knobs
    borderOutlines and separators
    text, mutedNormal text; placeholders and panel titles
    button, button_hover, button_pressedSecondary buttons and dropdowns
    accent, accent_hover, accent_pressed, accent_textPrimary buttons, selection, focus rings; text on accent
    trackSlider, progress and toggle tracks
    disabled, disabled_textDisabled widgets
    dangerEASYUI_DANGER buttons

    Example

    easyui.fillrect(x, y, w, h, easyui.theme()->surface);

    easyui.loadfont

    int easyui.loadfont(const char* path, int bold);

    Loads an OpenType (.otf, CFF outlines) or TrueType (.ttf) font file and uses it for every widget.

    ParameterDescription
    pathFont file, for example a resource of your app: "0:/programs/myapp/Resources/Font.ttf"
    bold0 for size-1 text, 1 for size 2 and larger. Load the same file into both to use one face everywhere

    Returns 1, or 0 if the file could not be read or is not a font the renderer understands (CID-keyed CFF, variable or colour fonts). The font already loaded stays in use when it fails.

    Notes Call it after init, which has already loaded Inter. The file is read into the heap and kept for the life of the program.

    Example

    if (!easyui.loadfont("0:/programs/notes/Resources/Mono.ttf", 0))
    mos_puts("using Inter\n");

    easyui.setsmoothtext

    void easyui.setsmoothtext(int on);

    0 draws every text with the 8 × 8 bitmap font even when a font is loaded (for a retro look, or pixel-exact layouts); 1 (the default) goes back to smooth text.

    easyui.smoothtext

    int easyui.smoothtext(void);

    Returns 1 if text is being drawn with an outline font, 0 if it is using the bitmap fallback.

    Example

    if (!easyui.smoothtext()) easyui.settext(status, "Install mosWM for nicer text");

    easyui.createbutton

    int easyui.createbutton(int x, int y, int w, int h, const char* text);

    A push button. By default it is filled with the accent colour; see easyui.setstyle for the other styles.

    ParameterDescription
    x, y, w, hBounds
    textLabel, centred; wraps onto several lines if it is too wide

    Returns the widget, or 0.

    Events ONPRESS, ONRELEASE, ONCLICK, ONCE, ONHOVER, ONLEAVE, ONFOCUS, ONBLUR, ONKEY.

    Example

    int save = easyui.createbutton(20, 20, 120, 36, "Save");
easyui.recallfunc(save, ONCLICK, save_file);

    easyui.createlabel

    int easyui.createlabel(int x, int y, int w, int h, const char* text);

    Text. It wraps at word boundaries to fit w, and \n starts a new line; the block is centred vertically in h. Change it with settext, its colour with setcolor, its size with settextsize and its alignment with setalign.

    Returns the widget, or 0.

    Notes Labels get ONCLICK too, which makes them usable as links.

    easyui.createslider

    int easyui.createslider(int x, int y, int w, int h, int min, int max, int value);

    A slider. It is horizontal, or vertical when h is greater than w (the top is max).

    ParameterDescription
    min, maxRange
    valueStarting value, clamped to the range

    Returns the widget, or 0.

    Events ONCHANGE with the new value whenever it moves (dragging, clicking the track, the mouse wheel, arrow keys or setvalue), plus ONPRESS / ONRELEASE around a drag.

    Example

    static void volume_changed(int value) { set_volume(value); }

int vol = easyui.createslider(20, 60, 200, 24, 0, 100, 50);
easyui.recallfunc(vol, ONCHANGE, volume_changed);
easyui.setstep(vol, 5);   /* arrow keys and wheel move by 5 */

    easyui.createcheckbox

    int easyui.createcheckbox(int x, int y, int w, int h, const char* text, int checked);

    A checkbox with a label to its right. Clicking anywhere on the widget toggles it.

    Returns the widget, or 0. Read the state with getvalue (1 or 0).

    Events ONCHANGE (1 / 0), ONCLICK.

    easyui.createradio

    int easyui.createradio(int x, int y, int w, int h, const char* text, int group);

    A radio button. Radio buttons with the same group number exclude each other: selecting one clears the others. The first one created in a group starts selected.

    ParameterDescription
    groupAny number you choose; one per set of choices

    Returns the widget, or 0.

    Events ONCHANGE with 1 on the button that became selected and 0 on the one that was cleared.

    Example

    static int small, medium, large;

static void size_picked(int selected) {
    if (!selected) return;                  /* ignore the one being cleared */
    int w = easyui.current();
    set_size(w == small ? 1 : w == medium ? 2 : 3);
}

small  = easyui.createradio(20, 20, 120, 24, "Small", 1);
medium = easyui.createradio(20, 48, 120, 24, "Medium", 1);
large  = easyui.createradio(20, 76, 120, 24, "Large", 1);
easyui.recallfunc(small, ONCHANGE, size_picked);
easyui.recallfunc(medium, ONCHANGE, size_picked);
easyui.recallfunc(large, ONCHANGE, size_picked);

    easyui.createtoggle

    int easyui.createtoggle(int x, int y, int w, int h, const char* text, int on);

    An on/off switch with a label. Behaves like a checkbox.

    Returns the widget, or 0.

    Events ONCHANGE (1 / 0), ONCLICK.

    easyui.createtextinput

    int easyui.createtextinput(int x, int y, int w, int h, const char* placeholder);

    A one-line text field. placeholder is shown in grey while the field is empty and not focused.

    Returns the widget, or 0.

    Events ONCHANGE after every edit (value: the new length), ONSUBMIT when Enter is pressed (value: the length), ONFOCUS, ONBLUR, ONKEY.

    Notes

    • Typing uses a US keyboard layout. Text is limited to 127 bytes, or less with easyui.setmaxlength.
    • easyui.setpassword shows * instead of the characters.
    • Read the text with gettext, change it with settext.

    Example

    static int search;

static void run_search(int length) {
    if (length) find(easyui.gettext(search));
}

search = easyui.createtextinput(20, 20, 260, 32, "Search");
easyui.recallfunc(search, ONSUBMIT, run_search);

    easyui.createprogress

    int easyui.createprogress(int x, int y, int w, int h, int max);

    A progress bar from 0 to max. Set it with setvalue; change the range with setrange.

    Returns the widget, or 0.

    Example

    int bar = easyui.createprogress(20, 20, 300, 10, total_files);
...
easyui.setvalue(bar, files_done);

    easyui.createdropdown

    int easyui.createdropdown(int x, int y, int w, int h);

    A drop-down list. Add choices with additem. Until one is selected it shows its text ("Choose..."; change it with settext). Clicking opens a list of up to 8 rows below it (above, if there is no room), which scrolls with the wheel.

    Returns the widget, or 0. getvalue is the selected index (-1 for none) and gettext the selected item's text.

    Events ONCHANGE with the selected index.

    Example

    int lang = easyui.createdropdown(20, 20, 200, 30);
easyui.additem(lang, "English");
easyui.additem(lang, "Svenska");
easyui.setvalue(lang, 0);
easyui.recallfunc(lang, ONCHANGE, language_changed);

    easyui.createlistbox

    int easyui.createlistbox(int x, int y, int w, int h);

    A scrolling list. Add rows with additem. Clicking a row selects it; the wheel scrolls.

    Returns the widget, or 0. getvalue is the selected index (-1 for none).

    Events ONCHANGE with the selected index, ONSUBMIT with the index on a double-click or Enter.

    Example

    static int files;

static void open_file(int index) { open(easyui.getitem(files, index)); }

files = easyui.createlistbox(20, 20, 240, 200);
for (long i = 0; i < n; i++) easyui.additem(files, entries[i].name);
easyui.recallfunc(files, ONSUBMIT, open_file);

    easyui.createpanel

    int easyui.createpanel(int x, int y, int w, int h, const char* title);

    A rounded box with an optional title in its top-left corner, for grouping widgets. Create it before the widgets that sit on it. setcolor changes its fill.

    Returns the widget, or 0.

    easyui.createimage

    int easyui.createimage(int x, int y, int w, int h, const uint32_t* pixels,
                       int image_w, int image_h);

    Shows an ARGB8888 image, scaled to w × h. Pixels with alpha below 255 are blended.

    ParameterDescription
    pixelsimage_w × image_h pixels, row by row. Not copied: keep the buffer alive while the widget exists
    image_w, image_hImage size

    Returns the widget, or 0.

    Notes After changing the pixels, call easyui.redraw(). Images get ONCLICK, ONPRESS and the hover events.

    easyui.createcanvas

    int easyui.createcanvas(int x, int y, int w, int h);

    An area you draw yourself. Its ONDRAW callback runs whenever the window is repainted, with drawing clipped to the canvas. Use the drawing calls below, in window coordinates.

    Returns the widget, or 0.

    Example

    static int chart;

static void draw_chart(int value) {
    int x = easyui.getx(chart), y = easyui.gety(chart), h = easyui.getheight(chart);
    for (int i = 0; i < 10; i++)
        easyui.fillrect(x + i * 20, y + h - data[i], 16, data[i], easyui.accent());
}

chart = easyui.createcanvas(20, 20, 200, 120);
easyui.recallfunc(chart, ONDRAW, draw_chart);

    easyui.createseparator

    int easyui.createseparator(int x, int y, int w);

    A one-pixel horizontal line in the border colour.

    Returns the widget, or 0.

    easyui.remove

    void easyui.remove(int widget);

    Deletes a widget and frees its items. Its number may be reused by the next create... call.

    easyui.recallfunc

    int easyui.recallfunc(int widget, int event, easyui_callback fn);

    Sets the function called when event happens on widget. Each widget has one callback per event; registering again replaces it.

    ParameterDescription
    widgetA widget, or EASYUI_WINDOW (0) for window events
    eventOne of the events
    fnvoid fn(int value), or NULL to remove the callback

    Returns 1, or 0 for an unknown widget or event.

    Example

    static void pressed(int v)  { easyui.settext(status, "Holding..."); }
static void released(int v) { easyui.settext(status, "Let go"); }

int button1 = easyui.createbutton(0, 0, 200, 100, "Click me!");
easyui.recallfunc(button1, ONPRESS, pressed);
easyui.recallfunc(button1, ONRELEASE, released);

    easyui.current

    int easyui.current(void);

    Returns the widget whose callback is running (0 for window events and timers).

    Example

    static void digit(int v) { append(easyui.gettext(easyui.current())); }

for (int i = 0; i < 10; i++) {
    char t[2] = { (char)('0' + i), 0 };
    easyui.recallfunc(easyui.createbutton(20 + i * 44, 20, 40, 40, t), ONCLICK, digit);
}

    easyui.settext

    void easyui.settext(int widget, const char* text);

    Changes the text of a button, label, checkbox, radio button, toggle, text input (the cursor moves to the end), panel title or the dropdown's "nothing selected" text. Longer text is cut at 127 bytes. Does not fire ONCHANGE.

    easyui.gettext

    const char* easyui.gettext(int widget);

    Returns the widget's text; for a dropdown or list box, the selected item's text. The pointer stays valid until the text changes. An invalid widget returns "".

    easyui.setvalue

    void easyui.setvalue(int widget, int value);

    Sets the value: a slider or progress bar position (clamped to the range), a checkbox or toggle (0 / 1), a radio button (1 selects it), or the selected index of a dropdown or list box (-1 for none). Fires ONCHANGE if the value changed.

    easyui.getvalue

    int easyui.getvalue(int widget);

    Returns the value described under setvalue.

    easyui.setrange

    void easyui.setrange(int widget, int min, int max);

    Changes a slider's or progress bar's range and clamps its value into it.

    easyui.setstep

    void easyui.setstep(int widget, int step);

    How far a slider moves per arrow key or wheel notch, and what dragging snaps to. Default 1.

    easyui.additem

    int easyui.additem(int widget, const char* text);

    Adds a row to a dropdown or list box. The text is copied.

    Returns the new item's index, or -1 if memory ran out.

    easyui.clearitems

    void easyui.clearitems(int widget);

    Removes every item and clears the selection (to -1).

    easyui.getitem

    const char* easyui.getitem(int widget, int index);

    Returns an item's text, or "" for an index out of range.

    easyui.itemcount

    int easyui.itemcount(int widget);

    Returns the number of items.

    easyui.setenabled

    void easyui.setenabled(int widget, int enabled);

    Disables (0) or enables (1) a widget. A disabled widget is drawn grey, cannot get focus and ignores clicks and keys.

    easyui.setvisible

    void easyui.setvisible(int widget, int visible);

    Hides (0) or shows (1) a widget. Hidden widgets get no events.

    Example

    /* simple tabs: show one page's widgets at a time */
for (int i = 0; i < page1_count; i++) easyui.setvisible(page1[i], tab == 0);

    easyui.setposition

    void easyui.setposition(int widget, int x, int y);

    Moves a widget.

    easyui.setsize

    void easyui.setsize(int widget, int width, int height);

    Resizes a widget.

    easyui.setanchor

    void easyui.setanchor(int widget, uint32_t anchors);

    Says which window edges the widget keeps its distance to when the window is resized. The default is EASYUI_ANCHOR_LEFT | EASYUI_ANCHOR_TOP: it stays put.

    AnchorsEffect when the window grows
    RIGHTMoves right with the right edge
    LEFT | RIGHTStretches horizontally
    BOTTOMMoves down with the bottom edge
    TOP | BOTTOMStretches vertically

    (Each name is prefixed with EASYUI_ANCHOR_.) The distances are measured when setanchor is called.

    Example

    int ok = easyui.createbutton(easyui.width() - 110, easyui.height() - 46, 90, 32, "OK");
easyui.setanchor(ok, EASYUI_ANCHOR_RIGHT | EASYUI_ANCHOR_BOTTOM);   /* stays in the corner */

    easyui.setcolor

    void easyui.setcolor(int widget, uint32_t argb);

    Gives one widget its own colour: the accent of a button, slider, checkbox, radio, toggle, progress bar, list or dropdown; the text colour of a label; the fill of a panel. Pass 0 to go back to the theme.

    easyui.settextsize

    void easyui.settextsize(int widget, int size);

    Text size, 1 … 8. With smooth text, size 1 is 12 px Inter Regular and size n (2 and up) is 8 × n px Inter Medium, as in mosWM. With the bitmap font, each size is 8 × n pixels tall. Checkbox, radio and toggle boxes and list rows grow with it.

    Example

    int title = easyui.createlabel(20, 10, 300, 30, "Settings");
easyui.settextsize(title, 2);

    easyui.setalign

    void easyui.setalign(int widget, int align);

    EASYUI_ALIGN_LEFT, EASYUI_ALIGN_CENTER or EASYUI_ALIGN_RIGHT, for labels and buttons. Buttons are centred by default, labels left-aligned.

    easyui.setstyle

    void easyui.setstyle(int widget, int style);

    A button's look:

    StyleLook
    EASYUI_PRIMARYFilled with the accent colour (default)
    EASYUI_SECONDARYGrey, like mosWM's Cancel buttons
    EASYUI_DANGERRed, for destructive actions
    EASYUI_FLATNo background until hovered; accent-coloured text

    Example

    easyui.setstyle(cancel, EASYUI_SECONDARY);
easyui.setstyle(delete_button, EASYUI_DANGER);

    easyui.setpassword

    void easyui.setpassword(int widget, int hidden);

    Shows a text input's characters as * when hidden is 1.

    easyui.setmaxlength

    void easyui.setmaxlength(int widget, int length);

    The most characters a text input accepts, at most 127.

    easyui.setimage

    void easyui.setimage(int widget, const uint32_t* pixels, int image_w, int image_h);

    Changes an image widget's pixels.

    easyui.setfocus

    void easyui.setfocus(int widget);

    Gives a widget keyboard focus (0 removes focus). Useful to put the cursor in a text input when the window opens.

    easyui.focused

    int easyui.focused(void);

    Returns the widget with keyboard focus, or 0.

    easyui.type

    int easyui.type(int widget);

    Returns the kind of widget: EASYUI_BUTTON, EASYUI_LABEL, EASYUI_SLIDER, EASYUI_CHECKBOX, EASYUI_RADIO, EASYUI_TOGGLE, EASYUI_TEXTINPUT, EASYUI_PROGRESS, EASYUI_DROPDOWN, EASYUI_LISTBOX, EASYUI_PANEL, EASYUI_IMAGE, EASYUI_CANVAS, EASYUI_SEPARATOR, or EASYUI_NONE for an invalid one.

    easyui.getx

    int easyui.getx(int widget);

    Returns the widget's left edge. gety, getwidth and getheight return the rest of its bounds, which change when anchors move it.

    easyui.gety

    int easyui.gety(int widget);

    Returns the widget's top edge.

    easyui.getwidth

    int easyui.getwidth(int widget);

    Returns the widget's width.

    easyui.getheight

    int easyui.getheight(int widget);

    Returns the widget's height.

    easyui.settimer

    int easyui.settimer(int interval_ms, easyui_callback fn);

    Calls fn every interval_ms milliseconds while run() (or update()) is running. The value passed is the timer number.

    Returns a timer number (1 … 8), or 0 if all timers are in use.

    Notes Timers run between frames, so their resolution is about 16 ms. To run something once, stop the timer in its own callback.

    Example

    static int clock_label;

static void tick(int timer) {
    char t[16];
    format_time(t, mos_uptime() / 1000);
    easyui.settext(clock_label, t);
}

easyui.settimer(1000, tick);

    easyui.stoptimer

    void easyui.stoptimer(int timer);

    Stops a timer from settimer.

    Example

    static void once_later(int timer) {
    easyui.stoptimer(timer);
    easyui.settext(status, "Ready");
}
easyui.settimer(2000, once_later);

    easyui.messagebox

    void easyui.messagebox(const char* title, const char* text);

    int ok = easyui.createbutton(20, 20, 100, 36, "OK");
easyui.setfontsize(ok, 16);
easyui.setradius(ok, 18);
int cancel = easyui.createbutton(130, 20, 100, 36, "Cancel");
easyui.copystyle(cancel, ok);
easyui.setstyle(cancel, EASYUI_SECONDARY);

    Text in your own pixels (font.h)

    font.h draws text into any ARGB8888 pixel buffer, for programs that render their own window contents (games, canvases, clocks) instead of using easyui widgets. It uses the same OpenType renderer and Inter fonts as mosWM and easyui, so text looks like the rest of MOSdesk: smooth and anti-aliased. When the fonts cannot be read (mosWM is not installed), it falls back to the 8 × 8 bitmap font, scaled by the text size.

    Header only; it can be included together with easyui.h.

    Functionsdraw_texttext_widthtext_heightfont_load
    #include "window.h"
#include "font.h"

static uint32_t pixels[320 * 120];

draw_text(pixels, 320, 120, 10, 10, "Score 120", 0xFFEAF2F8, 1);
int w = text_width("Game over", 2);
draw_text(pixels, 320, 120, (320 - w) / 2, 50, "Game over", 0xFFFFD166, 2);

    Sizes

    SizeSmooth textBitmap fallback
    112 px Inter Regular8 × 8
    2 and up8 × size px Inter Medium(8 × size) square glyphs

    These match easyui's text sizes and mosWM's own text.

    Functions

    draw_text

    void draw_text(uint32_t* pixels, uint32_t width, uint32_t height,
               int x, int y, const char* text, uint32_t color, int size);

    Draws text with its top-left corner at (x, y) into a width × height buffer whose rows are width pixels long. Clipped to the buffer. '\n' starts a new line. The color is 0xAARRGGBB; text is blended with the pixels underneath, so a lower alpha draws translucent text. Text is UTF-8; the bundled Inter files are a subset that may lack some characters, and the bitmap fallback has ASCII only.

    text_width

    int text_width(const char* text, int size);

    Width in pixels of the widest line, for centring and right alignment.

    text_height

    int text_height(int size);

    Height of one line (ascent + descent).

    font_load

    int font_load(const char* path, int bold);

    Uses another .otf / .ttf file instead of Inter: bold = 0 for size-1 text, 1 for size 2 and up. Returns 1 on success. Call it before the first draw_text.

    font_set_smooth, font_is_smooth

    void font_set_smooth(int on);
int font_is_smooth(void);

    font_set_smooth(0) always uses the bitmap font. font_is_smooth() says whether the OpenType fonts were found.

    Notes

    • The fonts are read from 0:/programs/mosWM/assets/fonts/ the first time text is drawn or measured (about 50 KiB of memory for both faces).
    • Glyphs are cached, so redrawing the same text every frame is cheap.
    • MOSdesk's Snake, Clock and Paint use it.

    Graphics

    Full-screen framebuffer access over SYS_GRAPHICS, for programs that take over the whole display instead of opening a mosWM window. The ownership, info, blit and present calls are in minimalos.h (from x86_64/user_common.h); the size queries and drawing primitives are in x86_64/user_graphics.h. Include graphics.h to get all of them plus the short graphics_* names.

    Most apps should use windows instead. Under MOSdesk, mosWM already owns the screen and a second program cannot acquire it.

    Functionsmos_graphics_acquiremos_graphics_releasemos_graphics_ownermos_graphics_infomos_graphics_blit_surfacemos_graphics_presentmos_graphics_get_widthmos_graphics_get_heightmos_graphics_clearmos_graphics_pixelmos_graphics_linemos_graphics_rectanglemos_graphics_fill_rectanglemos_graphics_trianglemos_graphics_fill_trianglemos_graphics_circlemos_graphics_fill_circlemos_graphics_ellipsemos_graphics_textmos_graphics_measure_textmos_graphics_set_resolutionmos_graphics_callmos_graphics

    How drawing works

    The kernel keeps a back buffer the size of the screen. A program:

    1. takes ownership of the screen with mos_graphics_acquire;
    2. draws into its own ARGB8888 surface (a malloced uint32_t array);
    3. copies the surface into the back buffer with mos_graphics_blit_surface;
    4. shows the changed rectangle with mos_graphics_present;
    5. gives the screen back with mos_graphics_release, which redraws the terminal.
    #include "graphics.h"
#include "stdlib.h"

int main(void) {
    if (mos_graphics_acquire() != SYS_SUCCESS) { mos_puts("screen busy\n"); return 1; }
    uint32_t w = mos_graphics_get_width(), h = mos_graphics_get_height();
    uint32_t* surf = malloc((size_t)w * h * 4);
    for (uint32_t f = 0; f < 300; f++) {
        for (uint32_t i = 0; i < w * h; i++) surf[i] = 0xFF000000 | ((i + f * 4) & 0xFF);
        mos_graphics_blit_surface(surf, w, h, w * 4, 0, 0, (int32_t)w, (int32_t)h, 0, 0,
                                  SYS_GRAPHICS_BLIT_OPAQUE);
        mos_graphics_present(0, 0, (int32_t)w, (int32_t)h);
        mos_sleep(16);
    }
    mos_graphics_release();
    return 0;
}

    Privilege

    On Minimal-OS a .run program is a user process, and the kernel only lets user processes call these graphics operations: get width, get height, owner, acquire, release, info, blit and present. The drawing primitives - clear, pixel, line, rectangle, circle, triangle, ellipse, text, measure text and set resolution - return SYS_ERR_PERM to a user process; they exist for kernel-privileged callers. Draw shapes and text into your own surface and blit it.

    The Run Studio preview runs the primitives for any program, so code that uses them works there but not on the real system.

    mos_graphics_acquire

    long mos_graphics_acquire(void);

    Makes the calling process the owner of the screen. Only the owner may blit, present, draw or read raw input.

    Returns SYS_SUCCESS, or SYS_ERR_PERM if another process owns the screen.

    Notes While a program owns the screen, keyboard and mouse input goes to the raw input queue (mos_input_read) instead of the terminal.

    mos_graphics_release

    long mos_graphics_release(void);

    Gives up ownership and redraws the terminal.

    Returns SYS_SUCCESS, or SYS_ERR_PERM if the caller does not own the screen.

    mos_graphics_owner

    uint64_t mos_graphics_owner(void);

    Returns the PID that owns the screen, or SYS_ERR_NOTFOUND if nobody does.

    Example

    if (mos_graphics_owner() != SYS_ERR_NOTFOUND) mos_puts("a desktop is running; open a window instead\n");

    mos_graphics_info

    long mos_graphics_info(syscall_graphics_info_t* info);

    Describes the display. The wrapper sets info->size, info->version and info->reserved before the call.

    syscall_graphics_info_t fieldMeaning
    width, heightScreen size in pixels
    pitchFramebuffer bytes per row
    pixel_formatBack-buffer format; always SYS_GRAPHICS_PIXEL_FORMAT_ARGB8888
    bytes_per_pixelFramebuffer bytes per pixel
    red_position, red_mask_size, and green/blueFramebuffer channel layout

    Returns SYS_SUCCESS, SYS_ERR_INVAL for a NULL or malformed structure, SYS_ERR_GENERIC if there is no framebuffer.

    Notes Surfaces you blit are always ARGB8888; the channel layout is only informative.

    mos_graphics_blit_surface

    long mos_graphics_blit_surface(const uint32_t* src, uint32_t width, uint32_t height,
                               uint32_t pitch, int32_t sx, int32_t sy, int32_t sw, int32_t sh,
                               int32_t dx, int32_t dy, uint32_t flags);

    Copies a rectangle of an ARGB8888 surface into the kernel back buffer. Nothing appears until mos_graphics_present.

    ParameterDescription
    srcSurface pixels, 4-byte aligned. The whole surface must be one live heap allocation of this process
    width, heightSurface size, 1 … 16384 each
    pitchSurface bytes per row: a multiple of 4, at least width × 4. pitch × height at most 64 MiB
    sx, sy, sw, shSource rectangle; must lie inside the surface and have positive size
    dx, dyWhere its top-left lands on screen; parts off screen are clipped
    flagsSYS_GRAPHICS_BLIT_OPAQUE copies pixels as they are; SYS_GRAPHICS_BLIT_ALPHA blends them using their alpha byte

    Returns SYS_SUCCESS, SYS_ERR_PERM if the caller does not own the screen, SYS_ERR_INVAL for any argument outside the rules above, SYS_ERR_GENERIC if the blit failed.

    Example

    /* draw a 32x32 sprite with transparency at (x, y) */
mos_graphics_blit_surface(sprite, 32, 32, 32 * 4, 0, 0, 32, 32, x, y, SYS_GRAPHICS_BLIT_ALPHA);
mos_graphics_present(x, y, 32, 32);

    mos_graphics_present

    long mos_graphics_present(int32_t x, int32_t y, int32_t width, int32_t height);

    Copies a rectangle of the back buffer to the visible framebuffer. The rectangle is clipped to the screen.

    Returns SYS_SUCCESS, SYS_ERR_PERM if the caller does not own the screen, SYS_ERR_INVAL for an empty rectangle or no framebuffer.

    Notes Present only what changed: a small dirty rectangle is much cheaper than the whole screen.

    mos_graphics_get_width

    uint32_t mos_graphics_get_width(void);

    Returns the screen width in pixels. Allowed for any process.

    mos_graphics_get_height

    uint32_t mos_graphics_get_height(void);

    Returns the screen height in pixels. Allowed for any process.

    mos_graphics_call

    long mos_graphics_call(syscall_graphics_request_t* request);

    Issues SYS_GRAPHICS with a filled syscall_graphics_request_t. The request has an op (a SYS_GRAPHICS_* value), an args[10] array of integers, and pointers for text, output sizes, blit and info. Every wrapper on this page builds one and calls this (or mos_graphics, its uint64_t twin in x86_64/user_syscalls.h).

    mos_graphics

    uint64_t mos_graphics(syscall_graphics_request_t* request);

    Same as mos_graphics_call, returning uint64_t.

    Input

    Raw keyboard and mouse input for programs that own the screen. Window apps do not need any of this: mosWM delivers key and mouse events to their window (see mos_window_next_event).

    mos_input_read is in x86_64/user_syscalls.h; the mouse calls are in x86_64/user_mouse.h and the USB keyboard calls in x86_64/user_usb.h.

    Functionsmos_input_readmos_mouse_get_statemos_mouse_pollmos_mouse_has_mousemos_mouse_initmos_mousemos_mouse_callmos_usb_has_keyboardmos_usb_key_to_asciimos_usb_key_is_pressedmos_usb_keyboard_infomos_usb_pollmos_usb_initmos_usb

    mos_input_read

    uint64_t mos_input_read(syscall_input_event_t* events, uint32_t capacity,
                        uint32_t timeout_ms, uint64_t* dropped_count);

    Takes queued keyboard and mouse events off the kernel's input queue. Only the screen owner may call it; while nobody owns the screen, hardware input goes to the terminal instead.

    ParameterDescription
    eventsArray to fill
    capacitySize of events, 1 … SYSCALL_INPUT_MAX_READ (256)
    timeout_msHow long to wait when the queue is empty, at most 5000. 0 returns at once
    dropped_countIf not NULL, receives the total number of events dropped because the queue was full

    Returns the number of events written (0 on timeout), SYS_ERR_PERM if the caller does not own the screen, SYS_ERR_INVAL for a bad argument.

    syscall_input_event_t fields:

    FieldMeaning
    typeSYSCALL_INPUT_KEY_DOWN, _KEY_UP, _MOUSE_MOVE, _MOUSE_BUTTON or _MOUSE_WHEEL
    keyUSB HID usage code (key events)
    modsSYSCALL_INPUT_MOD_SHIFT, _CTRL, _ALT bits
    buttonsSYSCALL_INPUT_BTN_LEFT, _RIGHT, _MIDDLE bits: the current button state
    dx, dyRelative motion (MOUSE_MOVE)
    wheelRelative scroll (MOUSE_WHEEL)
    time_msUptime when the event was queued

    Notes The queue holds SYSCALL_INPUT_QUEUE_CAPACITY (256) events. When it is full the newest event is dropped and the drop counter increases.

    Example

    syscall_input_event_t ev[32];
uint64_t n = mos_input_read(ev, 32, 16, NULL);   /* wait up to one frame */
if (n > 32) n = 0;                               /* an SYS_ERR_* value */
for (uint64_t i = 0; i < n; i++) {
    if (ev[i].type == SYSCALL_INPUT_KEY_DOWN && ev[i].key == 41) quit = 1;   /* Esc */
    if (ev[i].type == SYSCALL_INPUT_MOUSE_MOVE) { mx += ev[i].dx; my += ev[i].dy; }
}

    mos_mouse_get_state

    uint64_t mos_mouse_get_state(syscall_mouse_state_t* out_state);

    Reads the USB mouse's accumulated motion since the last call, and resets it. Screen owner only.

    syscall_mouse_state_t fieldMeaning
    dx, dyMotion since the last call
    wheelScroll since the last call
    buttonsCurrent SYSCALL_MOUSE_BTN_LEFT, _RIGHT, _MIDDLE bits

    Returns SYS_SUCCESS, SYS_ERR_PERM if the caller does not own the screen, SYS_ERR_INVAL for a NULL pointer.

    mos_mouse_poll

    uint64_t mos_mouse_poll(void);

    Polls the USB controllers once so new mouse reports are picked up.

    Returns SYS_SUCCESS.

    mos_mouse_has_mouse

    uint64_t mos_mouse_has_mouse(void);

    Returns 1 if a USB mouse is present, 0 if not.

    mos_mouse_init

    uint64_t mos_mouse_init(void);

    Initialises the USB mouse driver. Kernel-privileged: a .run program gets SYS_ERR_PERM.

    mos_mouse

    uint64_t mos_mouse(uint64_t operation, uint64_t arg1, uint64_t arg2);

    Issues SYS_MOUSE with a SYS_MOUSE_* operation. The functions above wrap it. mos_mouse_call in minimalos.h is the same call with long results.

    mos_mouse_call

    long mos_mouse_call(uint64_t operation, uint64_t arg1, uint64_t arg2);

    See mos_mouse.

    mos_usb_has_keyboard

    uint64_t mos_usb_has_keyboard(void);

    Returns 1 if a USB keyboard is attached, 0 if not.

    mos_usb_key_to_ascii

    char mos_usb_key_to_ascii(uint8_t scancode, uint8_t modifiers);

    Translates a USB HID usage code to a character using the active keyboard layout.

    ParameterDescription
    scancodeHID usage code, as in syscall_input_event_t.key or a window key event
    modifiersHID modifier byte: 0x02/0x20 left/right Shift, 0x01/0x10 left/right Ctrl, 0x40 AltGr. Caps Lock is applied by the kernel

    Returns the character, or 0 if the key has none (arrows, function keys).

    Example

    char c = mos_usb_key_to_ascii((uint8_t)ev.key, (ev.mods & SYSCALL_INPUT_MOD_SHIFT) ? 0x02 : 0);

    uint64_t mos_usb_key_is_pressed(uint8_t scancode);

    address, portUSB address and root-hub port
    stateDevice state in the USB stack
    vendor_id, product_idUSB IDs
    class_codeUSB class
    is_keyboard1

    Returns SYS_SUCCESS, SYS_ERR_NOTFOUND if there is no keyboard, SYS_ERR_INVAL for a NULL pointer.

    Polls the USB controllers once.

    Returns SYS_SUCCESS.

    Re-initialises and re-enumerates the USB controllers. Kernel-privileged: a .run program gets SYS_ERR_PERM.

    mos_usb

    Issues SYS_USB with a SYS_USB_* operation. The functions above wrap it.

    Edit this page on GitHub

    Networking

    IPv4 networking over SYS_NET: interface status, DNS, TCP clients and servers, UDP and the experimental ktls transport. Include net.h.

    Before a program can use the network the interface needs an address. Run dhcp in the terminal first; a .run program cannot do it itself (see mos_net_dhcp).

    Things to know about every call here:

    Functionsmos_net_statusmos_net_is_upmos_net_pollmos_net_resolvemos_net_lookupmos_net_dhcpmos_tcp_connectmos_tcp_sendmos_tcp_send_allmos_tcp_recvmos_tcp_recv_exactmos_tcp_statemos_tcp_closemos_tcp_listenmos_tcp_acceptmos_tcp_unlistenmos_tcp_handoffmos_udp_bindmos_udp_unbindmos_udp_recvmos_udp_recv_timeoutmos_udp_sendmos_tls_connectmos_tls_wait_establishedmos_tls_acceptmos_tls_statemos_tls_sendmos_tls_recvmos_tls_closemos_ip_parsemos_ip_to_stringmos_htonsmos_htonlmos_net_call
    • Host order. IPv4 addresses are uint32_t in host order (192.168.1.10 is 0xC0A8010A), and ports are plain numbers. You only swap bytes for values you put inside your own packets (mos_htons).
    • Polled. The kernel stack only makes progress when a process calls into it. A program that stops calling recv stops receiving. Loop with a short mos_sleep, or use the blocking helpers at the end of this page.
    • One at a time. The stack is not reentrant. A call that finds it in use by another process returns SYS_ERR_BUSY; retry it.
    • Handles. Connections, listeners, UDP bindings and TLS sessions are small positive integers in separate namespaces. They belong to the process that made them; a dead process's handles are closed the next time any process connects, listens or accepts.
    • No driver. With no network card every call except mos_net_status and mos_tcp_state returns SYS_ERR_GENERIC.

    A small HTTP client

    #include "net.h"
#include "stdio.h"

int main(void) {
    if (!mos_net_is_up()) { mos_puts("run dhcp first\n"); return 1; }
    uint32_t ip = mos_net_lookup("example.com", 5000);
    if (!ip) { mos_puts("lookup failed\n"); return 1; }

    long c = mos_tcp_connect(ip, 80, 5000);
    if (c <= 0) { printf("connect failed (%ld)\n", c); return 1; }

    const char* req = "HEAD / HTTP/1.0\r\nHost: example.com\r\n\r\n";
    uint32_t len = 0; while (req[len]) len++;
    mos_tcp_send_all(c, req, len);

    char buf[512];
    long idle = mos_uptime();
    for (;;) {
        long n = mos_tcp_recv(c, buf, sizeof buf - 1);
        if (n < 0) break;                                  /* closed */
        if (n == 0) {
            if (mos_uptime() - idle > 5000) break;
            mos_sleep(5);
            continue;
        }
        buf[n] = '\0'; mos_puts(buf); idle = mos_uptime();
    }
    mos_tcp_close(c);
    return 0;
}

    mos_net_status

    long mos_net_status(syscall_net_status_t* out);

    Reports the interface configuration. Never touches the stack, so it never returns SYS_ERR_BUSY.

    syscall_net_status_t fieldMeaning
    has_driver1 if a network card driver is loaded
    configured1 if the interface has an IPv4 address
    mac[6]MAC address
    local_ip, netmask, gateway, dnsHost-order IPv4 addresses

    Returns SYS_SUCCESS, or SYS_ERR_INVAL for a NULL pointer.

    Example

    syscall_net_status_t st;
char ip[16];
mos_net_status(&st);
mos_ip_to_string(st.local_ip, ip);
printf("address %s\n", ip);

    mos_net_is_up

    bool mos_net_is_up(void);

    Returns true if there is a driver and the interface has an address.

    mos_net_poll

    long mos_net_poll(void);

    Processes whatever the network card has received, once. Cheap; safe in a loop. recv, accept and udp_recv already poll, so most programs never call this directly.

    Returns SYS_SUCCESS, SYS_ERR_BUSY, or SYS_ERR_GENERIC with no driver.

    mos_net_resolve

    long mos_net_resolve(const char* hostname, uint32_t* out_ip, uint32_t timeout_ms);

    Looks up a host name with DNS.

    ParameterDescription
    hostnameName to resolve
    out_ipReceives the host-order address
    timeout_msHow long to wait; 0 means 5000

    Returns SYS_SUCCESS, SYS_ERR_NOTFOUND if the name did not resolve, SYS_ERR_GENERIC if the interface has no address, SYS_ERR_INVAL for a NULL argument, SYS_ERR_BUSY.

    mos_net_lookup

    uint32_t mos_net_lookup(const char* host, uint32_t timeout_ms);

    Accepts either a dotted-quad address or a host name.

    Returns the host-order address, or 0 on failure.

    Example

    uint32_t ip = mos_net_lookup(argc > 1 ? argv[1] : "10.0.2.2", 3000);

    mos_net_dhcp

    long mos_net_dhcp(uint32_t timeout_ms);

    Acquires an address with DHCP. Kernel-privileged: a .run program always gets SYS_ERR_PERM, because a lease changes the address for every process on the machine. Use the terminal's dhcp command.

    mos_tcp_connect

    long mos_tcp_connect(uint32_t ip, uint16_t port, uint32_t timeout_ms);

    Opens a TCP connection and waits for it to be established.

    ParameterDescription
    ipHost-order address, not 0
    portRemote port, not 0
    timeout_msConnect timeout; 0 means 5000

    Returns a connection handle (> 0), SYS_ERR_GENERIC if the connection failed or timed out, there is no address or no free handle, SYS_ERR_INVAL for a zero address or port, SYS_ERR_BUSY.

    mos_tcp_send

    long mos_tcp_send(long handle, const void* buf, uint32_t len);

    Sends up to 4096 bytes of buf.

    Returns the number of bytes sent, which can be fewer than len - a short count is not an error. SYS_ERR_BADFD for a bad handle, SYS_ERR_INVAL for a NULL buffer or zero length, SYS_ERR_GENERIC on failure, SYS_ERR_BUSY.

    Notes Use mos_tcp_send_all to send a whole buffer.

    mos_tcp_send_all

    bool mos_tcp_send_all(long handle, const void* buf, uint32_t len);

    Calls mos_tcp_send until all of buf is sent.

    Returns true when everything was sent, false as soon as a send fails.

    mos_tcp_recv

    long mos_tcp_recv(long handle, void* buf, uint32_t len);

    Reads whatever has arrived, without waiting.

    Returns the number of bytes read; 0 if nothing has arrived yet; SYS_ERR_NOTFOUND once the peer has closed and everything has been read; SYS_ERR_BADFD, SYS_ERR_INVAL or SYS_ERR_BUSY.

    Notes 0 means "try again later", not end of stream. Sleep a few milliseconds between empty reads.

    mos_tcp_recv_exact

    bool mos_tcp_recv_exact(long handle, void* buf, uint32_t len, uint32_t timeout_ms);

    Reads exactly len bytes, sleeping between empty reads.

    ParameterDescription
    timeout_msGives up after this long with no new data. The timer restarts whenever data arrives

    Returns true when len bytes were read, false if the peer closed or the timeout passed.

    Example

    uint8_t header[4];
if (!mos_tcp_recv_exact(c, header, 4, 2000)) goto fail;

    mos_tcp_state

    long mos_tcp_state(long handle);

    Returns one of SYSCALL_NET_TCP_CLOSED, _CONNECTING, _ESTABLISHED, _CLOSING or _PEER_CLOSED, or SYS_ERR_BADFD. Never returns SYS_ERR_BUSY.

    mos_tcp_close

    long mos_tcp_close(long handle);

    Closes the connection and frees the handle.

    Returns SYS_SUCCESS, SYS_ERR_BADFD or SYS_ERR_BUSY.

    mos_tcp_listen

    long mos_tcp_listen(uint16_t port, uint32_t backlog);

    Starts accepting connections on port.

    ParameterDescription
    portLocal port, not 0. Only one listener per port machine-wide
    backlogConnections to queue before accepting; 0 for a small default. Clamped by the kernel

    Returns a listener handle (> 0), valid only for mos_tcp_accept and mos_tcp_unlisten. SYS_ERR_INVAL if the port is 0 or already has a listener, SYS_ERR_GENERIC if there is no address or no free listener slot, SYS_ERR_BUSY.

    mos_tcp_accept

    long mos_tcp_accept(long listener, uint32_t* out_ip, uint16_t* out_port);

    Takes the oldest waiting client. Never blocks.

    ParameterDescription
    listenerHandle from mos_tcp_listen
    out_ip, out_portIf not NULL, receive the client's address and port

    Returns a connection handle (> 0); 0 if nobody is waiting (or every connection handle is in use); SYS_ERR_BADFD, SYS_ERR_BUSY.

    Example

    long ls = mos_tcp_listen(8080, 0);
for (;;) {
    uint32_t ip; uint16_t port;
    long c = mos_tcp_accept(ls, &ip, &port);
    if (c > 0) { serve(c); mos_tcp_close(c); }
    else mos_sleep(10);
}

    mos_tcp_unlisten

    long mos_tcp_unlisten(long listener);

    Stops listening and frees the listener handle. Connections already accepted stay open.

    Returns SYS_SUCCESS, SYS_ERR_BADFD or SYS_ERR_BUSY.

    mos_tcp_handoff

    long mos_tcp_handoff(long handle, uint32_t pid);

    Gives a connection you own to another process, typically a child started with mos_exec to serve it. The connection then closes when that process dies instead of when you do.

    ParameterDescription
    handleConnection handle you own
    pidNew owner, not 0

    Returns SYS_SUCCESS, SYS_ERR_PERM if you do not own the handle, SYS_ERR_BADFD, SYS_ERR_INVAL for pid 0.

    Notes The child needs nothing special: pass it the handle number on its command line and it can use it once the handoff is done. Until then the parent still owns it.

    Example

    char num[24]; /* format c into num */
const char* args[] = { num };
long pid = mos_exec("0:/programs/worker.run", args, 1);
if (pid > 0) mos_tcp_handoff(c, (uint32_t)pid);

    mos_udp_bind

    long mos_udp_bind(uint16_t local_port);

    Opens a UDP port for receiving (and as a default source port).

    Returns a UDP handle (> 0), SYS_ERR_INVAL for port 0, an error if the port is taken or all 4 bindings are in use, SYS_ERR_BUSY.

    mos_udp_unbind

    long mos_udp_unbind(long handle);

    Closes a UDP binding.

    Returns SYS_SUCCESS or an error for a bad handle.

    mos_udp_recv

    long mos_udp_recv(long handle, void* buf, uint32_t len,
                  uint32_t* out_from_ip, uint16_t* out_from_port);

    Takes the next queued datagram. Polls the card first; never blocks.

    Returns the datagram's length (bytes copied), 0 if none is waiting, SYS_ERR_BADFD, SYS_ERR_INVAL, SYS_ERR_BUSY.

    Notes A datagram larger than len is truncated and the rest is lost.

    mos_udp_recv_timeout

    long mos_udp_recv_timeout(long handle, void* buf, uint32_t len,
                          uint32_t* out_from_ip, uint16_t* out_from_port,
                          uint32_t timeout_ms);

    Waits up to timeout_ms for a datagram.

    Returns its length, 0 on timeout, or a negative error.

    mos_udp_send

    long mos_udp_send(long handle, uint32_t dst_ip, uint16_t dst_port,
                  uint16_t src_port, const void* buf, uint32_t len);

    Sends one datagram.

    ParameterDescription
    handleA UDP handle; used for its port when src_port is 0
    dst_ipDestination, or SYSCALL_NET_IP_BROADCAST for 255.255.255.255
    dst_portDestination port
    src_portSource port, or 0 to use the handle's
    buf, lenPayload, 1 … 1024 bytes

    Returns len, SYS_ERR_INVAL for an empty or oversize payload or no source port, SYS_ERR_GENERIC if sending failed or there is no address, SYS_ERR_BUSY.

    Example

    long u = mos_udp_bind(40000);
mos_udp_send(u, SYSCALL_NET_IP_BROADCAST, 40000, 0, "hello?", 6);
char reply[256]; uint32_t from; uint16_t fport;
long n = mos_udp_recv_timeout(u, reply, sizeof reply, &from, &fport, 2000);

    Notes Under QEMU's -netdev user the guest is behind NAT and LAN broadcasts never reach it; use a tap or bridge network to test discovery.

    mos_tls_connect

    long mos_tls_connect(uint32_t ip, uint16_t port, uint32_t timeout_ms);

    Opens a ktls session: a TCP connection plus a hello. The handshake finishes in the background.

    Returns a TLS handle (> 0) or a negative error.

    Notes ktls is a transport shape, not real TLS: there are no certificates and the session key crosses the wire in the clear. It does not talk to ordinary HTTPS servers and gives no security. (The terminal's wget uses the kernel's separate TLS 1.3 client.)

    mos_tls_wait_established

    bool mos_tls_wait_established(long handle, uint32_t timeout_ms);

    Polls mos_tls_state until the handshake completes.

    Returns true when established, false if it failed or timeout_ms passed.

    mos_tls_accept

    long mos_tls_accept(long tcp_handle);

    Turns a TCP connection you own into a server-side ktls session.

    Returns a TLS handle (> 0) or a negative error. On success the TCP handle must no longer be used (closing the TLS handle closes it); on failure it is still yours.

    mos_tls_state

    long mos_tls_state(long handle);

    Advances the handshake and reports the session state.

    Returns SYSCALL_NET_TLS_CLOSED (failed or closed), SYSCALL_NET_TLS_HANDSHAKING or SYSCALL_NET_TLS_ESTABLISHED, or a negative error (SYS_ERR_BUSY: retry).

    mos_tls_send

    long mos_tls_send(long handle, const void* buf, uint32_t len);

    Returns bytes sent (at most 4096 per call; short counts are normal), SYS_ERR_AGAIN while the handshake is still running, SYS_ERR_BUSY.

    mos_tls_recv

    long mos_tls_recv(long handle, void* buf, uint32_t len);

    Returns bytes read, 0 if nothing has arrived, SYS_ERR_NOTFOUND once the session is closed and drained.

    mos_tls_close

    long mos_tls_close(long handle);

    Closes the session and its TCP connection.

    Returns SYS_SUCCESS or a negative error.

    mos_ip_parse

    uint32_t mos_ip_parse(const char* dotted);

    Parses "a.b.c.d".

    Returns the host-order address, or 0 if the string is not exactly four decimal octets of 0-255.

    Example

    uint32_t gw = mos_ip_parse("10.0.2.2");   /* 0x0A000202 */

    mos_ip_to_string

    void mos_ip_to_string(uint32_t ip, char* out);

    Formats a host-order address as dotted decimal. out must hold at least 16 bytes.

    mos_htons

    uint16_t mos_htons(uint16_t v);

    Swaps the bytes of a 16-bit value (host to network order). mos_ntohs is the same function. Only needed for fields inside your own packet formats.

    mos_htonl

    uint32_t mos_htonl(uint32_t v);

    Swaps the bytes of a 32-bit value. mos_ntohl is the same function.

    mos_net_call

    long mos_net_call(syscall_net_request_t* request);

    Issues SYS_NET with a filled syscall_net_request_t. Every function on this page builds a zeroed request, sets op and the fields that operation uses, and calls this.

    System information

    Machine-wide statistics over SYS_SYSINFO. Include user_sysinfo.h. Every call is allowed for user programs, returns a uint64_t, and returns SYS_ERR_INVAL for an unknown query.

    Example - a one-line status bar:

    Functionsmos_sysinfo_cpu_usagemos_sysinfo_core_usagemos_sysinfo_core_countmos_sysinfo_ram_totalmos_sysinfo_ram_usedmos_sysinfo_ram_freemos_sysinfo_heap_usedmos_sysinfo_heap_freemos_sysinfo_pmm_used_pagesmos_sysinfo_pmm_free_pagesmos_sysinfo_uptime_msmos_sysinfo_process_countmos_cpu_hasmos_sysinfo
    #include "user_sysinfo.h"
#include "stdio.h"

int main(void) {
    printf("cpu %lu%%  ram %lu/%lu MiB  %lu cores  %lu procs  up %lu s\n",
           (unsigned long)mos_sysinfo_cpu_usage(),
           (unsigned long)(mos_sysinfo_ram_used() >> 20),
           (unsigned long)(mos_sysinfo_ram_total() >> 20),
           (unsigned long)mos_sysinfo_core_count(),
           (unsigned long)mos_sysinfo_process_count(),
           (unsigned long)(mos_sysinfo_uptime_ms() / 1000));
    return 0;
}

    mos_sysinfo_cpu_usage

    uint64_t mos_sysinfo_cpu_usage(void);

    Returns average CPU usage across all online cores, in percent (0-100).

    mos_sysinfo_core_usage

    uint64_t mos_sysinfo_core_usage(uint32_t core_id);

    Returns the usage of one core in percent, or SYS_ERR_INVAL if core_id is out of range or that core is not online.

    Example

    uint64_t cores = mos_sysinfo_core_count();
for (uint32_t i = 0; i < cores; i++)
    printf("core %u: %lu%%\n", i, (unsigned long)mos_sysinfo_core_usage(i));

    mos_sysinfo_core_count

    uint64_t mos_sysinfo_core_count(void);

    Returns the number of online cores.

    mos_sysinfo_ram_total

    uint64_t mos_sysinfo_ram_total(void);

    Returns total RAM in bytes.

    mos_sysinfo_ram_used

    uint64_t mos_sysinfo_ram_used(void);

    Returns RAM in use in bytes: kernel heap in use plus physical pages in use. An approximation.

    mos_sysinfo_ram_free

    uint64_t mos_sysinfo_ram_free(void);

    Returns ram_total - ram_used, or 0 if the estimate of used memory exceeds the total.

    mos_sysinfo_heap_used

    uint64_t mos_sysinfo_heap_used(void);

    Returns bytes allocated from the kernel heap, which also backs every program's malloc.

    mos_sysinfo_heap_free

    uint64_t mos_sysinfo_heap_free(void);

    Returns free bytes in the kernel heap.

    mos_sysinfo_pmm_used_pages

    uint64_t mos_sysinfo_pmm_used_pages(void);

    Returns physical 4 KiB pages in use.

    mos_sysinfo_pmm_free_pages

    uint64_t mos_sysinfo_pmm_free_pages(void);

    Returns free physical 4 KiB pages.

    mos_sysinfo_uptime_ms

    uint64_t mos_sysinfo_uptime_ms(void);

    Returns milliseconds since boot, the same value as mos_uptime.

    mos_sysinfo_process_count

    uint64_t mos_sysinfo_process_count(void);

    Returns the number of processes. To list them use mos_pslist.

    mos_cpu_has

    int mos_cpu_has(uint64_t mask);

    Returns 1 when every SYS_CPU_* feature in mask is usable, else 0. The AVX-family bits (SYS_CPU_AVX, SYS_CPU_AVX2, SYS_CPU_FMA, SYS_CPU_F16C, SYS_CPU_AVX512F and the other AVX-512 bits) are set only when the kernel enabled the register state (CR4.OSXSAVE and XCR0), so "1" means the instructions will not fault. They are 0 on a CPU without XSAVE/AVX and when the kernel was booted with the noavx flag, even though CPUID would still list them. Always test before running VEX or EVEX code; without the bit the instruction raises #UD and ends the program.

    The other bits are CPUID reports: SYS_CPU_SSE3, SSSE3, SSE41, SSE42, POPCNT, BMI1, BMI2, LZCNT, AES, PCLMUL, MOVBE, RDRAND, RDSEED, ADX, SHA. SSE2 is always there (x86-64).

    Example - choosing a code path:

    #include "user_sysinfo.h"

if (mos_cpu_has(SYS_CPU_AVX2 | SYS_CPU_FMA))
    render_avx2();          /* compiled with __attribute__((target("avx2,fma"))) */
else
    render_sse2();

    Compile only the functions that use AVX with __attribute__((target("avx2"))) (or -mavx2 for a separate file); the rest of the program must stay SSE-only so it runs everywhere. The kernel saves and restores all YMM/ZMM state around every system call, interrupt and context switch, so no extra care is needed between threads.

    mos_sysinfo_cpu_features, mos_sysinfo_xcr0

    uint64_t mos_sysinfo_cpu_features(void);   /* SYS_SYSINFO_CPU_FEATURES, 0x0C */
uint64_t mos_sysinfo_xcr0(void);           /* SYS_SYSINFO_XCR0, 0x0D */

    The raw feature mask (see mos_cpu_has) and the XCR0 value the kernel runs with: 0 without XSAVE/AVX, 7 for x87+SSE+AVX, 0xE7 with AVX-512.

    mos_sysinfo

    uint64_t mos_sysinfo(uint64_t op);

    Issues SYS_SYSINFO with a SYS_SYSINFO_* query, or SYS_SYSINFO_CORE_USAGE_BASE + core_id for one core. The functions above wrap it.

    Packages

    .mpkg archives over SYS_PKG. Include minimalos.h.

    An .mpkg holds files and directories, stored or LZSS-compressed. The terminal's pkg command and the dlr package client use the same calls.

    Functionsmos_pkg_unzipmos_pkg_zipmos_pkg_info

    mos_pkg_unzip

    long mos_pkg_unzip(const char* archive_path, const char* target_dir,
                   uint32_t* out_installed, uint32_t* out_failed);

    Extracts an archive into a directory.

    ParameterDescription
    archive_pathThe .mpkg file
    target_dirDirectory to extract into, for example "0:/"
    out_installedIf not NULL, receives the number of entries extracted
    out_failedIf not NULL, receives the number of entries that failed

    Returns SYS_SUCCESS if the archive was processed, SYS_ERR_GENERIC if it could not be read, SYS_ERR_INVAL for a NULL path or target.

    Notes Success means the archive was read; individual entries can still fail (invalid names are rejected, for one). Check out_failed.

    Example

    uint32_t ok = 0, bad = 0;
if (mos_pkg_unzip("0:/downloads/app.mpkg", "0:/", &ok, &bad) == 0)
    printf("installed %u entries, %u failed\n", ok, bad);

    mos_pkg_zip

    long mos_pkg_zip(const char* source_path, const char* algorithm,
                 char* out_path, uint32_t out_path_size);

    Archives a file or directory as <source_path>.mpkg.

    ParameterDescription
    source_pathFile or directory to pack
    algorithm"lzss", "store", or NULL for the default (LZSS)
    out_pathIf not NULL, receives the path of the archive written
    out_path_sizeSize of out_path

    Returns SYS_SUCCESS, SYS_ERR_GENERIC on failure, SYS_ERR_INVAL for a NULL source.

    Example

    char made[128];
if (mos_pkg_zip("0:/projects/game", NULL, made, sizeof made) == 0)
    printf("wrote %s\n", made);

    long mos_pkg_info(const char* archive_path, uint32_t* out_entry_count);

    Reads an archive's entry count without extracting it.

    Returns SYS_SUCCESS, SYS_ERR_GENERIC if the archive is invalid, SYS_ERR_INVAL for a NULL path.

    Device managers

    Calls into the kernel's GPU, audio, storage and USB managers over SYS_MANAGER. Include x86_64/user_managers.h.

    These exist for kernel-privileged code such as the boot sequence and the terminal. A .run program may only call mos_audio_has_data; every other operation returns SYS_ERR_PERM to a user process, because it reconfigures hardware the whole system shares.

    managerSYS_MANAGER_GPU, _AUDIO, _STORAGE or _USB
    operationSYS_MANAGER_INIT, _UPDATE, _START, _HAS_DATA or _SET_SAMPLE_RATE
    valueOperation argument (the sample rate), otherwise 0

    Returns the manager's result, or SYS_ERR_INVAL for an unknown manager or operation.

    PreviousPackagesNextFarcadeGL 3D

    Edit this page on GitHub

    FarcadeGL (farcadegl.h)

    FarcadeGL is the 3D library of Minimal-OS. It sits on the kernel's FGPU interface (SYS_GPU, described in fgpu_abi.h) and borrows from both OpenGL and Vulkan:

    On this pageHow it runsA first programContextsBuffers and vertex layoutsState and drawingBuilt-in programsShadersTexturesBlendingMathErrors and limitsPerformanceFunction referenceThe FGPU interface underneath
    • Like Vulkan, drawing is recorded into a command buffer and sent to the GPU in one call (fglSubmit / fglPresent). GPU memory is explicit: you create and destroy buffers, textures and shaders.
    • Like OpenGL, state is a handful of simple calls (fglEnable, fglUseShader, fglSetModel ...), matrices are column-major, and shaders are written in a GLSL-style language, FGSL (fgsl.md).

    It is header only: include farcadegl.h and build with ./build.sh.

    Contents:

    1. How it runs
    2. A first program
    3. Contexts
    4. Buffers and vertex layouts

    6. Built-in programs
    7. Shaders
    8. Textures
    9. Blending
    10. Math
